releases.notes: The first song of each set (Footloose, for the dancing) plays from its first note; Review still offers Llano's cut
The moving heads can be kept inside a box you set at each venue, so they never shine past it, and a Full power switch lets the dancing parts hit every light at full brightness.

A cue timeline on the Live screen: pause a song in Mixxx, see its parts and cues, add a white hit or a section at the red line, and nudge any cue earlier or later. Livin' on a Prayer has its white hits.

Moving heads now reach the whole room and Follow someone lands right on the person, brighter, and the Freedom Sticks go out bright in every look. Drops land with the music: a cut song keeps its original's phrases.
Dance songs now start where the dancing starts and end where it stops, so the floor no longer waits through a long intro. Review shows each song's Starts at and Ends at and lets you change them.
On the phone, Stop now works the moment you tap it, even while the Live screen is still drawing, with the heads section folded shut.

On the phone, the Live screen now opens on the party pads, with heads, levels and touch-a-light folded away underneath. On a smaller laptop screen the top cards now wrap their words instead of cutting them off.
Stage setup now keeps your Tetra numbering, with Tetra 1 on the right, instead of renumbering them left to right. The console now points you to the laptop's Shows page to build the night.

In the Show Designer you can turn any light in the room picture (a quarter turn, an eighth turn, or one degree at a time), and the turn is saved with the room. With no line-up yet, the GigBAR heads now face the dance floor. Update waits until you save a room you are still changing, and your line-up is kept when a room is redrawn.

On the Shows page, Get my songs now brings in your Drive song folder (only new or changed songs), and Add a song puts a song from this laptop into your show. Rebuilding the night is quicker because it redoes only songs that changed.
On the Shows page, Browse and Enter now say 'Still adding' while songs are coming in, instead of doing nothing.
Line up my lights now says how far apart the heads land in your room's feet or meters, and a saved show keeps its song folder and moment times after Llano Lights restarts.

Line up my lights now asks before you leave with unsaved changes, says what each switch does, and the room picture has a way back. Set up, the Setup guide and the Shows page answer every press plainly, like Stop saying Click again to stop and a save naming the show it made.

The run sheet now shows which Mixxx buttons are Enable Auto DJ and Fade Now, with a picture, and the Live screen and phone tell you what to press at each stop. The phone is safe to tap in a dark room, a loaded compilation always comes in fully filled, and the Shows page fixes are in.

Mixxx now plays the music and Llano Lights follows it, and the Live screen says so. Through the night the screen tells you what to press at every stop: no surprise Pause, and every hold waits for Fade Now.
Draw my room keeps your line-up so the heads face the floor, and slow sweeps glide smoothly instead of stopping half way
Tonight shows the night your show sets, the order and every song you added, before you build it, and it updates when the show changes
Hover follow follows only over the dance floor, and a quick move off it leaves the spot where you were following
Lining up on one or several spots never moves a GigBAR to the ceiling, and the room picture lands every beam on the spot you tap, the left side of the floor included
Line up my lights keeps a working line-up, a head turned the other way breaks nothing, and the room picture shows where the heads really point
The toasts and speeches now play your instrumentals in the order you set, with Sugar, Sugar still under the cake. The window also tells you when changes from Llano have landed and what each one was.

Moving heads now glide slowly over the floor by themselves in the first dance and father-daughter dance and stay off at dinner, and every screen has Stop heads and Take over. The night now follows the Nov 25 reception order, with a quiet background under the toasts and cake and a grand exit.
Load Mixxx now stops and tells you when it can't tell whether Mixxx is open, so it never changes Mixxx's library while Mixxx is running.

Shows now plan the whole night by part: cocktail hour and dinner each play a mood you pick, every Dancing song is tagged Hype, Dance or Slow, and Load Mixxx puts the built night straight into Mixxx. The moving heads only run by themselves during Dancing, and the room can be laid out as a stage venue by dragging.
A show now holds a whole wedding night, up to 120 songs instead of 60. Adding a folder whose songs are already in the show now tells you so instead of quietly redrawing everything.
A Setup guide now walks you step by step from plugging in the cables to a built night, checking each step for you as you go. It opens on its own the first time until you finish it or press Not now.
Pressing Stop after a live show no longer freezes the app. If the USB lights box is not plugged in you can still get into the app, and the lights pick up by themselves once you plug it in.

The Light studio Live screen is the front page: every look, color, spot and moment one tap away, the same console on your phone. The phone panel shows two codes: one joins the laptop's Wi-Fi with no typing, one opens Llano Lights.
Nothing changes in how the app looks or works; this release carries a real Windows check that the Shows Browse folder picker finds your folders.
The Start the laptop's own Wi-Fi button now answers right away and shows what Windows said; spot color dots light their own color, and the test-build banner can be dismissed.

Scene pads now hold all night and the newest press wins, a song's look plays before analysis finishes, the wedding night closes on the sing-along, Arrange the set no longer crashes, Photo mode holds steady, and wedding cues and phone moments hold their look.

Shows has a new panel, Build the whole night for Mixxx. It turns a wedding show into one folder Mixxx's Auto DJ plays: every song at one volume with a clean start and finish, a silent hold for each live moment (toasts, cake, the dances), numbered playlists in night order, a printable run sheet and a backup for your phone. You click Fade Now when a moment is over. A folder named Moments holds the dances' songs, and your original files are never changed.
The last dance now plays right before the night's final sing-along.

Shows has a new Arrange the set button. It puts a wedding playlist in an order that flows (cocktail hour, dinner, then the dancing with a hype opener, waves, a slow window and a sing-along close), gives every song a reason for its spot, shows the energy curve, and lets you drag songs to move them. Save as the show's order also sets the Mixxx playlist.
Each GigBAR card in the Show Designer now looks like the real bar, drawn from the Chauvet manual's front view, so you can tell at a glance which part of the bar is lighting up.
Spots you confirm now stay where you put them, and every light shows a position you can measure and change. The inner moving heads now pan along with the outer heads in slides.
Moving heads now hold their aim through a silence or a blackout instead of drifting. Line up my lights starts without the heads spinning, and you can hold an arrow to keep a head moving.
When a moving head has no measured positions, it now pans the same way as its partner on the bar, so the two heads move together instead of one going the wrong way.
Lights that start a move together now arrive together, and a light jumping from standing still no longer lurches ahead of the beat.
Head 4 now parks the short way, stays clear of its end stops and turns to face its spots, and the inner heads glide smoothly between positions.
Both moving heads now travel together, and the room picture in the window sweeps smoothly instead of stepping.
A laptop you leave open now checks for updates every half hour, so it picks up new builds like the smoother head moves without a restart.

The laptop follows Spotify and YouTube Music again with song names, and Local mode's hotspot and QR pairing are back; 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 had lost them. Everything new in 1.16.0 is here: Line up my lights on one screen, the GigBAR head fix, and Spotlight cues.

Line up my lights puts every light on one screen so all the heads aim at one spot, the GigBAR heads no longer get mixed up, and there are new Spotlight cues. Slow head moves no longer tick; they hold, then make one short smooth move.
Stop the show from your phone with no internet, and from llano.app or the Conductor
Moving heads now glide smoothly to a new spot instead of jumping. There is a new Power-up check, and you can tap the room picture to aim a light.

Center all now points every light at the floor, beams move smoothly in the room picture, and the Light doctor can work out a moving head from your taps. Updates now always restart the app, and if one fails it tells you why.
Every part of each GigBAR now shows up by name in Control a light, and the 4 strobes on each bar really flash. Lights on can now light the whole bar at once.
Pick tonight's rig before you start, Stop always answers, and a stuck MIDI controller or ENTTEC can no longer freeze the app.

The lights now come on while you line up and calibrate, calibration is kept once you save it, and every GigBAR channel can be set. If Lights crashes, the report it saved keeps going to Llano until Llano confirms it has it.

Llano now designs your show's looks and the laptop keeps them, so a saved show plays with no internet. Line up my lights has its own view where you can calibrate each GigBAR head so the picture matches the real beams, and the app opens faster with a timing Reset.

Shows: pick a playlist and it designs the whole night's lights song by song; play it, adjust it, save it by name. One phone app for internet and local, installable from Chrome. Both GigBARs' spots face the dance floor, Stop sits in the header, Test each light works, and Control a light sets any light by hand. (1.9.0 to 1.10.1 were never released on their own; they ship inside 1.11.0.)

Local mode: the laptop runs the show from its own hotspot with no internet, and your phone keeps control; opening Llano Lights again now brings the open window forward instead of starting a second copy.
Scene pads, white-out, blackout and party mode on the real lights; line-up check, open space, feet, undo, beat light, safer Stop and the rest of your 15 requests.
Lights now follow Spotify and YouTube Music in the browser: the show hears the laptop's sound, finds the beat, and reads the song name for its style. Mixxx still wins when it is playing.
Plays the show you describe on llano.app/lights, offline: per-section moves, levels, derby and laser, styles per song, and Play on laptop for drafts. The default show is unchanged.
The demo's intros change color every 4 bars instead of staying red, long intros move like a groove, and jumping to the start or switching songs no longer flashes a rainbow.
Link the laptop to llano.app/lights and change the show from there or by asking the Conductor; it keeps running on its saved settings offline.

Setup makes this the one Llano Lights: closes older copies, points old shortcuts here, lists it in Settings > Apps, and says Installed or exactly what failed. The demo's calm parts pulse on the beat and change color, and the demo has a seek bar with 10 second skips.
Opens only its own window: no more Edge windows or extensions. A Check for updates button next to the version. Its own Llano Lights icon in the title bar and taskbar.
The demo plays real music: three free songs and a song picker; the lights follow each song's beat and sections.
Shows its version and build time, and lists itself in Windows Settings > Apps with an Uninstall that asks before deleting your saved layouts.
Its own window: every mode is a button, Stop leaves the lights dark. Updates install themselves from here on, signed so only ours are accepted.
Show Designer fixes: saved layouts that would not open, save errors shown, no freeze on a tall room.
Show Designer: lay out your room so the movers aim at it and the chases run in order.
Renamed from GigBAR Lights to Llano Lights. Setup says when it did not finish instead of always reporting success.
GigBAR Lights: fixes to the first package and a new install guide.
First Windows package, as GigBAR Lights: nothing to install, a numbered menu, Demo, the Mixxx beat link and ENTTEC output, and a preview of all 12 lights.
